summary: Configured node1 to export `/srv/nfs/shared` to node2 and mounted it persistently at `/mnt/shared`. Both nodes use `dataops` UID/GID 4500; the shared directory is 4500:4500 mode 2770. Two-way writes preserve ownership and permissions. Both nodes were restarted serially and fully recovered with changed boot identities, persistent services/mounts, and intact data.
actions_performed: Installed Alpine NFS packages on both nodes.
Created `dataops` with UID/GID 4500 on both nodes.
Configured node1's export for node2 with `rw,sync,no_subtree_check` and default `root_squash`.
Enabled `rpcbind` and `nfs` at boot on node1.
Configured node2's persistent NFS mount and enabled `nfsmount` at boot.
Verified two-way file creation as `dataops`, producing UID/GID 4500:4500 and mode 664.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually, proving changed boot identities and full recovery after each restart.

evidence.requirement: Shared dataops identity with UID/GID 4500 on both nodes
evidence.summary: Both nodes report dataops as UID 4500 and GID 4500, including after their respective restarts.

evidence.requirement: Node1 exports `/srv/nfs/shared` with owner dataops:dataops and mode 2770
evidence.summary: Shows the active export, directory owner/group 4500:4500, mode 2770, active NFS service, and post-restart persistence.

evidence.requirement: Node2 mounts the export persistently at `/mnt/shared`
evidence.summary: Shows the live NFSv4.2 mount, persistent fstab entry, enabled nfsmount service, and automatic recovery after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Files created on either system retain consistent ownership and permissions
evidence.summary: Files created from both server and client are mutually readable and consistently retain UID/GID 4500:4500 and mode 664, including new writes after both restarts.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 2a087080-34ad-4bf1-b673-0840a72fd129; restart was acknowledged; new boot ID e89d580e-e7a7-490c-b9d4-93b906be497f was observed. NFS services, export, metadata, data, client access, and post-restart writes recovered.

Healthy baseline used boot ID f4d2b1cc-2826-4244-8e0b-6b9398794862; restart was acknowledged; new boot ID f31cc401-c082-41b5-9975-7e73d90fc1f9 was observed. The mount, identity, metadata, existing data, and new client write recovered and were confirmed on node1.
